body:
## Summary

The sidecar/provider transport accepts `http://` for **any host**, not just loopback, and then attaches the provider API key as a bearer token. Config validation requires only that the URL be a string — there is no scheme restriction, no host restriction, and no warning for a non-loopback plaintext endpoint.

An operator who points `extract.url` (or `embed.url` / `rerank.url`) at a remote `http://` endpoint sends a long-lived provider API key **and** the memory text being embedded or extracted in cleartext.

**Severity: Low–Medium.** It requires an operator configuration choice, but a "local sidecar" default is being silently extended to arbitrary remote hosts with no guard.

## Affected code

| Location | Role |
|---|---|
| `crates/clio-index/src/http.rs:71-80` | `HttpEndpoint::parse` accepts `http://` for any host, not only loopback |
| `crates/clio-index/src/http.rs:252` | embed request attaches `authorization: Bearer {key}` |
| `crates/clio-index/src/http.rs:285` | health-probe path attaches the same header |
| `crates/clio-config/src/config/validate.rs:254-266` | `embed.url` / `rerank.url` / `extract.url` validated as string only |

## Reproduction

Bytes captured off a socket by the real client:

```
[parse] accepted remote http:// -> host=api.vendor.example.com port=80 path=/v1/embed

[wire]   POST /v1/embed HTTP/1.1
[wire]   accept-encoding: gzip
[wire]   content-length: 48
[wire]   user-agent: ureq/3.4.2
[wire]   host: 127.0.0.1:60360
[wire]   content-type: application/json
[wire]   authorization: Bearer sk-live-VENDORKEY-abc123
[wire]
[wire]   {"input":"confidential memory text","model":"m"}

[wire] provider API key appeared in cleartext on the wire: true
[wire] confidential request payload in cleartext           : true
```

Real code exercised: `clio_index::HttpEndpoint::parse`, `clio_index::post_json`.

## Impact

- **Secret disclosure.** The provider API key traverses the network in cleartext and in the cleartext request body.
- **Content disclosure.** The memory text being embedded or extracted is readable by any network observer.
- **Integrity.** The request can be read and modified in transit, so an on-path attacker can alter the embedding/extraction input or response.

## Note on scope

The response side is handled well: `read_capped` (`crates/clio-index/src/http.rs:209-233`) enforces a 64 MiB cap, and TLS verification is in place for `https://` with optional custom root CA. This issue is specifically about the *request* side and the missing scheme/host guard.

## Proposed fix

- Require `https://` for any non-loopback host.
- Warn — or refuse — on `http://` to a remote address at configuration time, mirroring the loopback-only rule the MCP HTTP bind already enforces at `crates/clio-mcp/src/http.rs:90-96`.

That rule is a good precedent: the codebase already understands that a non-loopback listener needs protection. The same reasoning applies to an outbound non-loopback plaintext endpoint.

## Related

- #20 — plaintext triple SPO survives compliance erasure (the at-rest counterpart to this in-transit gap)
title: [security:low] Provider API key and memory payload sent over cleartext http:// to any host
